title: BOS discusses upcoming data center town hall, Seeley sidewalks & Gateway Water Treatment Plant | Local News | thedesertreview.com
text:
EL CENTRO — The Board of Supervisors discussed an upcoming data center town hall and heard an overview of public works projects during the regular meeting on Tuesday, March 17.
Town Hall
Chair Peggy Price said that the county will hold the data center town hall in the evening on Thursday, March 26 at 6 p.m. in the board chambers on 940 W. Main St.
“Many residents would like the Board of Supervisors to be present in the discussions regarding the Imperial Data Center project,” Price said. “We want to be clear that the board is not taking any action on the project at this meeting.
"Because this is an active application that may come before the board for future consideration, supervisors must remain impartial and cannot express positions on the project," she continued.
Price said that during this special meeting, the project applicant will provide a presentation on the proposed data center, followed by an opportunity for public comment.
The applicant will address questions related to the specifics of the project, Price added, and county staff will respond to questions regarding Imperial County processes related to the data center application.
“The purpose of the item is to receive information and to hear from the public, not to deliberate or make a decision,” Price said. “Supervisors can listen to the presentation and ask clarifying procedural or informational questions.
"Supervisors cannot express support or opposition, weigh in on the merits of the project, signal how they might vote or engage in back-and-forth advocacy with speakers.”
The county previously held a workshop about AI data centers in January. At that event, county executive officer Dr. Kathleen Lang said that the workshop was “intended as an informational and collaborative discussion” and said it was “not related to any data center project, nor is it a public hearing on any specific project.”
Public Works Projects
Public Works director David Dale gave an overview of county public works projects that are either in progress or coming to a close.
Dale said the department is wrapping up the $13 million Niland Wastewater Treatment Plant project, which spanned several years in planning and construction. The project was funded through a community development block grant from the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Housing and Community Development.
The $3 million Gateway Water Treatment Plant improvement project, funded through the American Rescue Plan Act and the Gateway Benefit Impact Fund, is also coming to a close.
This project replaced 18-year-old constant-speed pumps with new energy-efficient variable-speed pumps, which adjusted pumping speeds based on pressure fluctuations in the system. This endeavor also improved the plant’s electrical system and added a new emergency standby diesel generator to provide emergency power for the pumps.
Dale said Public Works is beginning the Seely Sidewalk Improvement Project, which is in the design phase. One project which is coming to an end is the Bowker improvement initiative from McCabe to Ross Rd., which received $1.5 million in Surface Transportation Block Grants.
“Also, we have the Drew Road Bridge where we are looking at some alternative designs to retrofit that will hopefully cut the cost of a brand new bridge by 80 percent or more,” Dale said of this structure which spans the New River south of the Rio Bend RV and Golf Resort and was closed for emergency repair in 2019.
In his concluding remarks, Dale highlighted a soccer field the Public Works staff installed at Sunbeam Lake Park, saying the crew turned a dirt lot into a new grass field.
“It takes a team, and we really do appreciate everyone working together to bring us forward and collaborating with all the different departments,” Price concluded.
